issues.legal_issue: The factum of a customary adoption is established by evidence showing a clear adoption intention and the adopter’s subsequent acknowledgment and treatment of the adoptee as a son.
material_facts: A formal deed recited the adoption and the adopter’s intention to treat the adoptee as his son.
The adopter made public declarations of the adoption and treated the adoptee as his adopted son, who enjoyed the rights of a son.
issues.conclusion: The evidence was ample to sustain the finding that the adoption had in fact occurred.
issues.legal_principle: The Court accepted the concurrent findings on factum based on the adoption deed and the adopter’s subsequent conduct; it applied no separate statutory provision or earlier case to this issue.

rule.if: adoption_validity_challenge and formal_deed_records_adoption and adopter_publicly_acknowledged_adoption and adopter_treated_adoptee_as_son

predicates.adoption_validity_challenge: A civil proceeding challenges whether an adoption occurred or is valid.
predicates.formal_deed_records_adoption: The adopter executed a formal deed recording the adoption.
predicates.adopter_publicly_acknowledged_adoption: The adopter publicly declared that the adoptee had been adopted.
predicates.adopter_treated_adoptee_as_son: The adopter treated the adoptee as his son.

issues.definition: When an adoption is challenged, a formal deed recording it, the adopter’s public acknowledgment, and his treatment of the adoptee as a son support finding that the adoption occurred.

issues.legal_issue: An adoption under customary law is not invalid merely because the adoptee is a distant collateral when the custom’s reference to near collaterals is ambiguous and directory rather than a clear mandatory restriction.
material_facts: The adopter belonged to a community governed by customary adoption rules whose stated object was to appoint an heir.
The applicable customary-law record referred to adoption of near collaterals but did not define the term or specify a degree of relationship.
The record left the right of selection to the adopter.
The adoptee was a collateral in the eighth degree, and the challengers asserted that only a near collateral could be adopted.
issues.conclusion: The adoption of the distant collateral was valid; the customary-law entry was directory, not mandatory, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Punjab customary law, adoption is secular in character and principally serves to appoint an heir; rules about ceremonies and preferences in selection are directory, and disregard of them does not invalidate an adoption. A custom derogating from the general custom must be proved in clear and unequivocal language. The Court relied on Question 9 of the Gurdaspur Riwaj-i-am and referred to Jiwan Singh v. Pal Singh (22 P.R. 1913, p. 84), Sant Singh v. Mula (44 P.R. 1913, p. 73), Chanan Singh v. Buta Singh (A.I.R. 1935 Lah. 83), Jowala v. Dewan Singh (166 I.C. 237), and Basant Singh v. Brij Raj Saran Singh (I.L.R. 57 All. 494). It contrasted customary adoption with adoption under Hindu law, which has a religious object, and noted the directory approach to certain preferences in Hindu-law texts described by Mulla, including the principle of factum valet.

rule.if: customary_adoption_challenge and adoption_serves_to_appoint_heir and custom_uses_undefined_near_collateral_term and adopter_has_selection_discretion and adoptee_is_distant_collateral and mandatory_restriction_not_clearly_proved

predicates.customary_adoption_challenge: A proceeding challenges the validity of an adoption governed by customary law.
predicates.adoption_serves_to_appoint_heir: The adoption’s object is to appoint an heir and provide a temporal family benefit.
predicates.custom_uses_undefined_near_collateral_te: The applicable custom refers to near collaterals without defining the term or specifying a degree of relationship.
predicates.adopter_has_selection_discretion: The applicable custom leaves the choice of adoptee to the adopter.
predicates.adoptee_is_distant_collateral: The person adopted is a distant collateral of the adopter.
predicates.mandatory_restriction_not_clearly_proved: The evidence does not establish in clear and unequivocal terms that the custom imposes a mandatory restriction on the choice of adoptee.

issues.definition: When a customary-adoption challenge concerns an heir-appointing adoption, an undefined reference to near collaterals leaves selection to the adopter, and no mandatory restriction is clearly proved, adoption of a distant collateral is valid.
